source.publication: Publication 120 Retirement Income (December 2025), with the 2025 IL-1040 Instructions and Form IL-1040
source.section: Pub 120 PDF page 2 'What retirement income may I subtract', PDF page 3 'What federally taxed income may I not subtract'; Form IL-1040 Line 5; Instructions PDF page 7, Line 5; Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 60,000.00 + Roth conversion (person 0) 200,000.00 = 260,000.00. Federal taxable income = 260,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 244,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 260,000.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 260,000.00. Line 5 Roth conversion 200,000.00 = 200,000.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 200,000.00. Line 9 base income = 260,000.00 - 200,000.00 = 60,000.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 260,000.00 is greater than 250,000.00, so the whole Line 10 allowance is removed. Line 10a 0.00. Line 10b 0.00. Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 0.00. Line 11 net income = 60,000.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 12 tax = 60,000.00 x 4.95% = 2,970.0000. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 2,970.00. The conversion is subtracted in full, yet it lifts federal AGI over 250,000.00 and so removes the allowance; the wages are taxed with no exemption.
